videos.title: How Din Tai Fung's Soup Dumplings Took Over The World
videos.overview: If you’re the kind of person who really loves your steamed Chinese soup dumplings then there’s a better than average chance you’ve heard of Din Tai Fung. Over the past few decades, the chain and its famous xiaolongbao soup dumplings have achieved semi-legendary status everywhere from Asia to Europe to the U-S. So what’s the secret sauce?

videos.title: What Ever Happened To Tang?
videos.overview: Tang is a vitamin-enhanced, powdered breakfast drink that -- once upon a time -- was practically synonymous with NASA and the astronauts of the U-S space program. And if you’ve ever wondered how a random fruit drink mix got its name attached to one of the most prestigious endeavors in the history of science, then stick around.

videos.title: The Top Pizza Chain In Every Region In America
videos.overview: No one has ever gotten into a fistfight over which of the big pizza chains is the best - defending the honor of Pizza Hut just isn’t worth a fist to the eye. But everyone has that one hometown pizza chain you’d go to the mat for. But which one is TRULY the best?

videos.title: Why The Hell Is It Called Ruth's Chris Steak House?
videos.overview:
Before it was a nationwide steak empire with a tongue-twister name where you go to impress your in-laws or celebrate a big raise…

There was just a guy named Chris, a sizzling steak, and a tiny restaurant in New Orleans. That is until a Ruth-less and savvy business woman managed to change things forever.

This is the beefy, buttery, slightly burned-at-the-edges origin story of Ruth’s Chris Steak House, a name so confusing, you’d think someone lost a bet. Turns out, the story is even more interesting than that.

videos.title: Were Warheads Ever ACTUALLY Dangerous?
videos.overview: If you were ever a kid in a candy store, odds are you know exactly which candy to grab a handful of if you’re aiming to scratch that sour itch. A moderate sour craving could be satisfied with a pack of sour patch kids or maybe a box of lemonheads. But for those candy thrill-seekers who really wanted to pucker up, the only solution was sour Warheads. Warheads are as delicious as they are.. terrifying!

videos.title: The Death Of The Ice Cream Parlor
videos.overview:
Some of the best childhood memories happened in the ice cream parlor. Birthdays, big team victories and special occasions all seem much better when someone behind the counter is asking “one scoop or two?” or “haven’t you had enough free samples yet?”

But despite all the sweet, delicious memories, when the heck was the last time you even saw an ice cream parlor, let alone stepped inside one? Do ice cream parlors even still exist?

videos.title: Why Doesn't Banana Flavor Taste Like Bananas?
videos.overview: Banana flavoring. Just hearing those words probably triggers a specific memory. Maybe it’s that weirdly chewy piece of Laffy Taffy you made a trade for during school lunch. Maybe it’s the smell of a banana popsicle you tried once and never fully recovered from. Or maybe it’s Circus Peanuts. No, really - we’ll get there. The point is, banana is one of the most ubiquitous flavors in desserts and candy. So how come none of it actually tastes like bananas?

videos.title: Are Kraft Singles Actually Cheese?
videos.overview: When Kraft Singles came onto the scene in the mid-20th century, they seemed too good to be true. Households across the US were delighted at a low cost cheese option that simply refused to spoil. Until the questions started coming in. What is this stuff? How can sliced cheese stay good for so long? Is it actually food?

videos.title: Why Nothing Else Tastes Like A McDonald’s Bun
videos.overview: When we’re horking down our favorite drive-thru burger, most of us aren’t thinking about the bun. But the bun is vital to the entire burger experience - it's the first thing you taste, setting the stage for the rest of the sandwich. And if everything isn’t perfect, it can throw off the whole sandwich. So how is it that a fast food place like McDonald’s seems to get it right every time?

videos.title: Why Pizza Pockets Completely Owned The ’90s
videos.overview: For kids in the 90s, there were few better microwave meal options than the noble Hot Pocket. A simple turnover stuffed with pizza, the Hot Pocket inspired as much loyalty as fear among its fans, as its ability to burn the hell out of your mouth became the stuff of schoolyard legend. But where did they come from? Who invented this lava-filled rectangle of raditude? How many times did you scorch your moth eating these? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: Why Is Everyone Obsessed With This Gas Station?
videos.overview: Forget what you know about gas stations—Buc-ee’s is more than a truck stop, it’s a full-blown roadside attraction. Known for its immaculate bathrooms, smoked brisket, wall-to-wall snacks and souvenirs, and a beaver mascot with surprising star power, Buc-ee’s is a must-visit destination. People plan entire road trips around it, driving hours just to grab a T-shirt or a kolache. So how did a simple stop-and-fuel become a destination vacation?

videos.title: Is Coke Zero Better For You Than Diet Coke?
videos.overview:
It’s a hot summer day and you want a cool, tasty beverage with absolutely no sugar or carbs anywhere in sight, and water simply will not do.

So you reach for a Diet Coke, but then notice the bottle of Coke Zero Sugar next to it, and that’s when the confusion sets in. Which should you get? Is one better than the other? Is there even a difference?

videos.title: The REAL Reason That Tipping Became A Thing
videos.overview: Even to those raised in a culture where it’s the norm, the practice of tipping can often seem downright random. Why do we tip some service providers for their efforts, but not others? Why are some jobs allowed to pay so little as long as there’s the expectation that tips will cover the rest? And who exactly made all these unspoken rules?

videos.title: Is Luxury Bottled Water Really Better Than Regular Bottled Water?
videos.overview: The average American drinks more than 45 gallons of bottled water per year. That’s a lot of water and a LOT of bottles. It seems especially jarring considering we get the same amount of water from our taps for the low, low price of our utility bill. But at some point, bottled water not only became popular, it was downright hip. So hip, in fact, that designer water became something advertising companies assured us we cannot do without. Fancy bottles, sparkling waters from the far reaches of the earth and even major bling has taken over the bottled water industry and turned it into the next top fashion. But is bougie, top-shelf bottled water actually any better for you than the stuff that comes out of your faucet? Which Do YOU Drink? Let Us Know in the comments!

videos.title: What Was The Most Popular Burger Of Each Decade?
videos.overview: Burgers have been a staple in lunch and dinners since their inception around the turn of the 20th century. Since that time, burgers have evolved, morphed and grown over the decades to become one of the most popular and most competitive foods in the country, with new styles and trends popping up regularly to transform the entire industry. But what were all those decade-defining burgers? The ones everyone and their brother couldn’t wait to order?

videos.title: Is This Soda Actually Good For You?
videos.overview: Walk into a grocery store today and you’ll probably find a can of something called probiotic soda, the biggest health-food hit in the soda aisle since sparkling water and Diet Coke. But what exactly is a probiotic soda supposed to do for you? And are they actually good for your health, or just another low calorie flash in the pan?

videos.title: Everything That Went Wrong With Panera Bread
videos.overview: When your tummy is rumbling for something fancy and the local fast food joints just won’t cut it, you can do worse than stopping by your local Panera Bread. When the doors open, you’re hit with a dozen smells of fresh bread, bubbling soups and sweet treats from the bakery all cooking an upscale meal for incriminating tastebuds. While Panera has the reputation of a higher-quality, fast casual dining experience, one has to wonder just how much can you expect to pay for two slices of bread, some meat and a bowl of soup?

videos.title: Everything That Was Fake About Kitchen Nightmares
videos.overview: Gordon Ramsay has made a career out of screaming at people, and rescuing their struggling businesses. Kitchen Nightmares remains one of the celebrity chef’s most popular shows in America, following Ramsay as he helps transform restaurants on the edge of bankruptcy into successes. But how real ARE those nightmares, and how much is played up for the cameras?

videos.title: Classic Lunchbox Juices That Almost Killed Us
videos.overview: While most of us coasted through childhood in a veritable sugar haze, it turns out all the fruit punches, apple juices and colorful elixirs we were throwing back in the cafeteria didn’t always have our good health in mind. But how can drinks that taste vaguely like fruit be bad for us?

videos.title: The Strange Reason Sour Patch Kids Are Shaped Like Children
videos.overview: Sour Patch Kids are gummy candies that -- for some reason -- are shaped like human children. Uh, sort of. Have you ever stopped to wonder why these sour treats look like a tiny person with a radical haircut? Who decided that was a good shape for candy?

videos.title: Why Nothing Tastes As Good As A McDonald's Hash Brown
videos.overview: It’s 8:47 a.m. You’re running late and you’re wearing sunglasses indoors. You didn’t plan to go to McDonald’s, but somehow you’ve wound up in the drive-thru, whispering your order like it’s a confession. And then it hits you. That smell. That sizzle. That little paper sleeve holding a golden, crispy oval that absolutely did not need to go that hard. McDonald’s hash browns aren’t just good. They’re emotional support potatoes. How often do you eat them? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: What Even Is "Flamin' Hot" Flavor?
videos.overview: Flamin’ Hot Cheetos are more than just a snack. For years, this radioactive red chip has captivated spice-lovers, confused parents, inspired music videos, and even sent kids to the hospital. And the backstory? It has everything: a rags-to-riches janitor-turned-executive tale, a corporate mystery worthy of a Netflix docuseries, and a brand so spicy it sparked a food revolution.

videos.title: Why Cream Soda Never Hit The Big Time
videos.overview: Cream Soda, the beverage that was designed to be a dessert in drink form, was one of the original soda recipes. Once an iconic staple of pharmacy soda shops across America, this retro beverage still keeps a dedicated fanbase, but it’s nowhere nearly as popular as Coke or Pepsi. So what happened? ...Do you drink Cream Soda? IF so, what's YOUR favorite? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: How MrBeast's Feastables Worked When it Absolutely Should Have Failed
videos.overview: Would you buy a feast from a beast? What if that beast were “Mister Beast” and that feast was a Feastables chocolate bar? If you said yes, you’re not alone. The Feastables snack line has been an unmitigated triumph for Mister Beast -- even though celebrity-based products have a disastrous hit rate. So how did he zig where everyone else zagged? What Do Yoy think about Feastables? Have you ever had one? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: Why Are Juice Boxes Only For Kids?
videos.overview: The juice is loose! Or it would be, if it weren’t contained by those miraculous contraptions we call juice boxes. The handy packages are a ubiquitous part of school lunches throughout much of the world, and we all love them for it. But how did they infiltrate our lunchboxes to become one of the biggest staples of childhood? What Were Some of YOUR Favorites? Let Us Know in the Comments!

videos.title: Why The Biggest Mexican Restaurant Of The '80s Suddenly Vanished
videos.overview:
It’s a Friday night in 1987and you’re wearing your best acid washed jeans with your Frankie Says Relax shirt. Your date’s hair has reached full Aqua Net structural integrity and you just slid into a red vinyl booth at Chi-Chi’s with a basket of free chips and a cold, syrupy margarita the size of a birdbath.

Chi-Chi’s wasn’t just a restaurant. It was where Midwest families went to feel spicy.

videos.title: What ACTUALLY Happened To Fruitopia
videos.overview: If you grew up in the early aughts, odds are you had a Fruitopia machine in your school. They just seemed to appear one day in the 90s as if from nowhere, offering fruity nectar of the gods to anyone brave enough to gaze upon the kaleidoscope imagery of its glowing display. While many may not remember Fruitopia and even fewer have actually tried it, for a time it was on top of the world. So why did it get tossed out of paradise?

videos.title: Why Are Continental Breakfasts Only At Hotels?
videos.overview: Road weary families looking for a quick place to lay their heads for the night want to wake up refreshed and ready to take on the day, and nothing does that quite like free orange juice and danishes in the little room next to the ice machine. Any hotel worth its weight in mini-muffins aims to please their clientele with a continental breakfast.

videos.title: Are There Actual Clams In Clamato Juice?
videos.overview: Clamato Juice is a beverage with a name that implies it’s made from a combination of clams and tomatoes and designed to prank your friends into chugging what they think is cloudy fruit punch. But are there really shellfish in that strange, bottled elixir? And who in their right mind would drink it on purpose?

videos.title: Is Annie’s Mac And Cheese Better For You Than Kraft Mac And Cheese?
videos.overview:
If you’re a fan of macaroni and cheese, and not cooking for yourself, then there’s a good chance you’ve heard of Annie’s Homegrown.

Buoyed by its health related claims, the company has managed to turn its flagship product into one of the biggest brands in the U-S. But how did they climb to the top so fast? And are their cheesy noodles truly a more health-conscious choice?

videos.title: Why Is Everyone Obsessed With This Seafood Spice?
videos.overview: No seafood boil is complete without the right seasoning. And everyone from the Mid-Atlantic knows that the "right seasoning" is Old Bay. But how has this simple spice bland cemented itself as a seafood staple? And when did people start using it on popcorn, potato salad, and around the rim of Bloody Marys?

videos.title: Is Celsius Better For You Than Red Bull?
videos.overview: Celsius is part of the next wave of energy drinks marketed toward fitness-minded adults, particularly women. It’s a pick-me-up in a can that’s made a name for itself by being the healthy alternative to “gamer fuel” like Monster and Red Bull. But is it really any better for you than a standard energy drink, or is it all just a bunch of red bull?

videos.title: Is Gas Station Sushi Safe To Eat?
videos.overview: Sushi! It’s delicate. It’s delicious. It’s got raw fish in it. And for many Americans, it’s absolutely terrifying when you see it sitting next to a taquito roller at a Shell station. But is gas station sushi really the intestinal minefield it’s made out to be? Or has it been a hidden catch of the day all along?

videos.title: Why Your Favorite "Health" Drink Is Not Healthy At All
videos.overview: “Naked Juice” may sound like something they have to mop off the floor after shooting an adult movie, but fortunately for us all, that’s not the case. It’s actually a line of fruit juices, protein smoothies, fruit smoothies and other similar beverages; and if you have any questions about the brand, you’re in luck, because today we’re going to take a look at the naked truth about Naked Juice.

videos.title: How Soda Fountains Took Over America
videos.overview:
We don’t typically drink milk or juice out of fountains, but for some reason, the soda fountain remains one of the dominant distribution systems for soft drinks.

In fact, if you’ve left your house in the past fifty years, you’ve likely noticed that pretty much every fast food joint, convenience store and movie theater now has one. How did soda fountains manage to conquer virtually all of food service?

videos.title: Classic Lunchbox Snacks That Almost Killed Us
videos.overview: When you were a kid at school, nothing beat the moment you could finally crack open your lunchbox and see what awesome treats your parents packed away for you… or which ones you snuck in there yourself when they weren’t looking. But while those lunchbox snacks were always a delight, they weren’t always healthy. In fact, several could be called delicious slow acting poisons!

videos.title: The Ice Cold Death Of The Choco Taco
videos.overview: The Choco Taco wasn’t just an ice cream treat, it was a culinary miracle. A frozen Frankenstein’s monster of a dessert that dared to ask, “What if a taco… but ice cream?” And for nearly 40 years, the answer was always: “Yes. Absolutely.” It wasn’t fancy. It wasn’t gourmet. But the Choco Taco’s unique design was the ice cream sandwich we’d all been dreaming of.

videos.title: How Long Does Beef Jerky ACTUALLY Stay Good?
videos.overview: On a long car ride or while pulling an all-nighter, few snacks hit like a good package of beef jerky. The tough, salty, sometimes spicy meat seems to last forever and never loses its kick. Once a necessity for our pioneer ancestors traveling across a tumultuous country, beef jerky remains a time-honored treat for anyone craving meat but not willing to cook it. So how did it become THE go-to snack of road trips throughout history?

videos.title: Why Nothing Else Tastes Like Baja Blast
videos.overview: It’s teal. It’s tropical. It’s the only soda that somehow tastes like both summer vacation and the floor of a Taco Bell at 1 a.m. For 20 years, Baja Blast has been more than just a drink — it’s a cult, a lifestyle, and one more thing for people to argue about on social media. But what is Baja Blast, really? How did it go from a limited-time Taco Bell exclusive to a year-round grocery store staple? And why does it have more spinoffs than CSI?

videos.title: The Red Hot Rise Of Nashville Hot Chicken
videos.overview: You hear about it on food blogs, restaurant advertisements and even in Jack Black’s Lava Chicken Song in A Minecraft Movie. Hot Chicken, forged in the fiery pits of Nashville’s hottest stovetops and available at any establishment that isn’t afraid to live life on the spicy side. Nashville Hot Chicken seemed to pop up overnight. So, where did it come from? And how did it take over our taste buds?

videos.title: Everything That Went Wrong With Blimpie
videos.overview: These days, when most people are hungry for a sandwich they head to places like Subway, Panera Bread, Jimmy John’s, Jersey Mike’s, or maybe even Firehouse. But once upon a time, not too long ago, the first name in sandwich shops was Blimpie. It even sounds delicious, like you’re going to get a whole lot of sammie for your buck. So what made this once-giant franchise go the way of the Hindenburg?

videos.title: The Secret Behind Red Lobster's Cheddar Bay Biscuits
videos.overview: When Red Lobster first opened its doors in 1968, it promised a “harbor for seafood lovers,” so you’d think their most popular dish would be, well… seafood. If not specifically lobster. But as anyone who’s ever sampled from their menu can tell you, the best thing on it is -- by far -- the Cheddar Bay Biscuits.

videos.title: How Combos Became The Ultimate Road Trip Snack
videos.overview: Combos - those little pretzel rolls with an assortment of savory fillings - seemingly came out of nowhere to dominate road trip snack discussions forevermore. But despite being one of the undisputed kings of convenience store pit-stops for the past several decades, there’s surprisingly little information about Combos out there. So how did these humble tubes of dough and cheese come out of obscurity to change long car rides forever?

videos.title: Why All Restaurants Suddenly Look The Same
videos.overview: Once upon a time, McDonald’s looked like McDonald’s, Taco Bell looked like Taco Bell, and White Castle looked like a place everyone but college kids wanted to avoid. But at some point, those chains started ditching their own styles in favor of a minimalist design that’s so samey, you can barely tell one place from the other.

videos.title: Why Vanilla Coke Failed (Then Came Back)
videos.overview:
Vanilla Coke wasn’t just a soda, it was a revelation. A sugary slap to the taste buds that whispered, “Hey, what if your Coke was just a little fancier? A little creamier? A little more vannilla-y?” It tasted like someone poured a melted Coke float into a bottle and said, “You’re welcome, America.” And for a while it was available in every movie theater, vending machine, and corner store.

Then all of a sudden, it was gone. What happened? Where did it go? Is it ever coming back?

videos.title: How Homer Simpson Saved Donuts
videos.overview: Look, we may not want to admit it, but every one of us is guilty of doing something just because we saw it on television. But that doesn’t always mean doing suplexes in your living room or burning the house down - sometimes, that just means scarfing down your favorite characters’ favorite foods. From the Ninja Turtles and E.T., to Garfield and Homer Simpson, every major pop culture character has a major signature snack. But have these iconic snackers unknowingly convinced us all to become eaters of their favorite treats? Is our willpower truly so low?

videos.title: Why Everything Tasted Better In The 90s
videos.overview: Not to come off like one of those old people who think everything was better back in their day, but… everything was better back in our day; our day being the nineties. Movies were better, music was better, and food was better. Not necessarily better for you; it just tasted better. And if you’re wondering why that is, you’re in luck.

videos.title: Everything That Went Wrong With Sbarro
videos.overview: For decades, Sbarro was the beating heart of the mall food court — a brand so tied to suburban adolescence that it’s basically shorthand for “killing time before the movie starts.” But while it once reigned supreme as the undisputed king of the food court jungle, Sbarro eventually became a punchline: mocked for its quality, gutted by bankruptcies, and immortalized as the butt of an Office joke.

videos.title: Why Does Some Food Taste Better As Leftovers?
videos.overview:
Open any fridge in America and you’ll find two things: a condiment that expired in 2012, and a mysterious Tupperware you’re too scared to open.

But here’s the twist — sometimes those forgotten meals actually taste better the next day.

videos.title: How Peasant Food Became Fine Dining
videos.overview:
Historically speaking, when you think about fine dining, you probably think about kings, queens, lords, ladies, and all other manner of aristocrats.

What you probably don’t think of is peasants. Yet, these days, so-called “peasant food” is increasingly considered fancy.

videos.title: Pepsi Blue Never Actually Went Away
videos.overview: There have been some major soda brands that have delighted MILLIONS over the decades! Coke, Mountain Dew, 7Up!... Many have tried variations of tried and true beloved concoctions, but, let's be honest - NOBODY saw Pepsi Blue coming. What IS Pepsi Blue, and how did it come about? What does it taste like? maybe you have had one?

videos.title: Why Endless Shrimp Was The Dumbest Deal In Restaurant History
videos.overview: People love seafood! ...And Shrimp. LOTS of Shrimp - Garlic shrimp, breaded shrimp, dipping in shrimp cocktail or melted butter. Big restaurant chains recognized this, and many of the bigs such as Red Lobster started offering customers 'Endless shrimp' deals... What could go wrong? As time went on, they quickly found out - their financial well being got stuck in a downward spiral, with HEAVY losses. Were you ever able to part-take in endless shrimp deals while they were offered? How many do you think YOU ate?

videos.title: The Deadliest Foods People Actually Eat
videos.overview: Some people out there like to live life EXTREME. Some folks enjoy the thrill of leaping out of an airplane. Others climb mountains or brave the wilderness for no other reason than it’s dangerous. But some decide to have their danger served to them on a platter, maybe with a side of fries and some sauce for dipping. There’s nothing exciting about a cheeseburger, but what if that cheeseburger had a 1 in 10 chance of taking you out in the most painful way possible? Isn’t that worth even a little taste?

videos.title: How Chicken Took Over McDonald's
videos.overview: There are few items on the McDonald’s menu more classically Micky D’s than the six-piece chicken McNugget. But if you’re wondering why a place known for burgers and fries is always looking for the next big chicken sensation, then stick around.

videos.title: The REAL Reason Pringles Come In A Can
videos.overview: With its one-of-a-kind, cardboard tube, metal bottom and plastic lid, Pringles are one of the most uniquely packaged snacks around. But it has to make you wonder: If that tube technology is really all that great, then why is Pringles the only chip makers that use it for their packaging?

videos.title: How Can Costco Afford To Give Away So Many Free Samples?
videos.overview: It begins the way all great weekend stories do, a card check, a concrete warehouse floor, and a tiny paper cup of microwaved meatball skewered on a toothpick. This is Costco, and at Costco, the samples are free. But how does it work? Who pays for those little bites of joy? It’s a mystery, for sure.

videos.title: Is Chicago Deep Dish Actually Pizza?
videos.overview: Pizza. It’s the number one food on the planet. Ok, maybe not literally. But, we can all agree that it’s in every human being’s top five, right? Like, who can say 'No' to pizza? Seems simple enough until you remember that according to some, pizza comes in both New York style and Chicago style. Have you ever HAD Chicago Style 'Deep Dish pizza? Which is YOUR favorite style?

videos.title: How Bennigan's Tried To Be Applebee's . . . And Lost Everything
videos.overview: Remember after-work happy hours with neon green cocktails, the “flair” era, and a sandwich so over-the-top it came with powdered sugar and jam? Well… that was Bennigan’s — America’s mall-pub for Monte Cristos and two-for-ones. But today, you’d be hard pressed to find one.

videos.title: Every Style Of Steak We Could Find
videos.overview: Humans have been eating beef and game since the prehistoric era, so steak has been on the dinner menu since, well… pretty much forever. From open fires to fine dining, its evolution has been shaped by economics, politics and time. So if the question is: Where’s the beef? The answer is: We found it, and then some!

videos.title: Is Expired Food Actually Dangerous?
videos.overview:
It’s 2 A-M. You’re starving. You shuffle into the kitchen like a zombie with one goal: vanilla yogurt. You find it. You cradle it. You whisper sweet nothings to it. But then… betrayal. It expired six days ago.

Do you eat it? Will it kill you? Is this how your autopsy report begins?

videos.title: Every Celebrity Liquor Brand We Could Find
videos.overview: Once upon a time, liquor was made and sold by people with names like Jim Beam and Jack Daniels. But these days, it’s more like The Rock and Ryan Reynolds. Yes, it suddenly feels like every celebrity you’ve ever heard of is out there pimping their own brand of booze.

videos.title: Is "Organic" A Scam?
videos.overview: The organic food business is driven by a desire for healthier meals, anxieties over the environment, and nostalgia for a time before chemical pesticides and fertilizers. But does organic food actually address any of those concerns? Or are we all just a bunch of suckers.

videos.title: Does $1,000 Pizza Actually Taste Better Than $1 Pizza?
videos.overview: From Naples street food to Michelin-level creations, pizza’s been around longer than there have been dollar bills to spend on it. So how did we get to the point where some pizza still costs just a single bill, while others pay thousands and thousands for a single slice?

videos.title: Is it Safe To Eat At A C Grade Restaurant?
videos.overview: Food poisoning. Cross-contamination. Clandestine societies of hungry rats. These are just a few of the many pressing concerns shared by restaurant-staff and consumers alike.  But, thanks to state-wide safety regulations, foodies can turn to restaurant grading systems to help decide where it’s safe to dine. But if A is excellent, and B takes a pass…What’s the risk in grabbing a bite from C?

videos.title: Why Orbitz Was Too Weird To Survive
videos.overview: Back in the nineteen-nineties, there was one drink that dared to ask: what if your beverage looked less like soda and more like a lava lamp? That drink was Orbitz — a short-lived, jelly-bead-filled curiosity that confused shoppers and terrified dentists. Have YOU ever had an Orbitz drink? Would you ever want to taste one of those ever again?

videos.title: The Strange Rise Of BuzzBallz
videos.overview: They look like bath bombs, taste like liquid candy, and hit like a heavyweight boxer. Whether you’ve downed one at a tailgate, or just stared at them in the liquor aisle, BuzzBallz have become impossible to ignore. But how did these party spheres take over the drinking world?

videos.title: How Paul Newman Accidentally Started A Food Empire
videos.overview: Given that he’s one of the most iconic movie stars of all time, it’s natural to wonder why Paul Newman’s name and likeness has long been used to sell bottles of salad dressing. Was he desperate for cash? Did he owe a favor to a friend? Was he being blackmailed by some evil salad dressing baron? Well, wonder no more.

videos.title: Everything There Is To Know About Sushi Rolls
videos.overview: Over a thousand years ago in Southeast Asia, people preserved fish by wrapping it in rice and letting it ferment. The Japanese then took that idea, refined it, and turned it into one of the most desired – and Instagram worthy – foods on the planet. But few realize quite how many varieties of sushi there really are!

videos.title: What's Actually In A Marshmallow
videos.overview: A campfire and cereal box staple that goes back a heck of a lot longer than most people realize, marshmallows are soft, squishy and rich in delicious marsh. Or is it mallow? The truth is, while most people love the taste of marshmallows on their smores, sweet potato pie, or in their cereal, few know exactly what lurks within them.

videos.title: How Margaritaville Became The Weirdest Business Empire In America
videos.overview: It started as a laid-back anthem about wasting away on the beach with a salty rimmed cocktail. But Jimmy Buffett’s *Margaritaville* didn’t stay a song for long. It transformed into a sprawling empire including things like restaurants, resorts, and yes… even pickleball sponsorships.

videos.title: The Strange Reinventions Of Slice Soda
videos.overview:
Slice was an iconic brand… a soda for the ages! Or at least that's what Pepsi wanted their definitely-not-Sprite-clone to be. And for a hot minute, it worked.

In the mid 1980’s, Slice was everywhere. It was everyone's go to drink of choice, until… it wasn’t. But once a brand name is well known, it never truly disappears. So, tell us, did you drink Slice in the '80s? Or how about the probiotic reboot? What did you think?

videos.title: The Unfortunate Downfall Of Hot Dog On A Stick
videos.overview: Hot Dog on a Stick is not just a sentence, but the name of an iconic establishment and also a description of an article of food. And yet, this once mighty delectable treat no longer dominates the economic hierarchies of mall food courts the way that it did in the 1980s.

videos.title: What Happens When All Of The Waiters Disappear?
videos.overview: Artificial intelligence has people everywhere wondering whose jobs are next — Writers? Developers? Maybe even yours. But one industry’s already feeling it: restaurants, where touchscreens and robot servers are quietly taking over. have YOU ever been served by a Robot? Have you taken your own order on a flatscreen at a fast food joint? Where Was it? Any hiccups in your worder?

videos.title: The Street Foods That Define Every Country
videos.overview: In the abstract, food that’s prepared in the street might strike some as less than appetizing. But in reality, there’s something magical about street food. So in honor of all the hungry folks, standing in the road for the chance to buy something hot, fresh, and fast… What was some of the best street food you ever had? Where was it? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: How In-N-Out Ruined Their Own French Fries
videos.overview: With their sprawling secret menu, a cult-worthy following of fanatic foodies, and pure devotion to drive-thru craftsmanship, In-N-Out just might be the most infamous regional burger chain in America. But while these shake-slinging masters know exactly what a hamburger is all about, one fast-food essential is seriously slacking. Because when it comes to In-N-Out, does anyone actually want fries with that?

videos.title: What Actually Is Wasabi?
videos.overview: Picture a vivid green smear next to your sushi roll. The tiny kick-in-the-nose that makes your eyes water and your date question your life choices. Yes, we’re talking about wasabi. It’s one of the world’s most misunderstood condiments, but that stops right now. So, what are your thoughts on Wasabi? Have you had the real thing? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: The Truth About Chick-fil-A
videos.overview: Ah, Chick-fil-A, the only place where you can order chicken nuggets and waffle fries, with a heaping side of Christian guilt. They’re known for customer service, drive-thru lines rivaling In-And-Out, and some pretty universally beloved fried chicken, but if you’re wondering how a family-owned diner turned into a billion chicken empire, stick around. So, do you love Chic-Fil-A? Do you have issues with the company? Let us know in the comments where you stand!

videos.title: What Prison Meals Really Look Like
videos.overview: From horrifying Hollywood cliches of disgusting cafeterias, to the slightly more palatable offerings at real-world commissaries, prison meals are a hot topic for the morbidly curious. But with so many terrible true-crime dining tales, one has to wonder: is prison food really that bad?

videos.title: Why Everyone's Obsessed With Mexican Birria Right Now
videos.overview: If you’re into online food trends, you’ve probably heard of Birria, the Mexican stew with an origin story that involves conquistadors, an army of goats, and an active volcano. But if you’re wondering what it really is about birria that’s got the internet so hyped up, stick around.

videos.title: The Best Foods To Eat At Every NFL Stadium (AFC Edition)
videos.overview: Attending an N-F-L game means dealing with attempts from the audience to break decibel measurements, long lines out of the parking lot, and overpriced beer. But there’s one thing that makes it all worth it. No, not the actual game, you can watch that from home. We are of course talking about the food.

videos.title: The Weird McDonald's Spin-Off That Failed Miserably
videos.overview:
In 2023, McDonald’s was looking for a way to stay relevant and capture the caffeine-crazy, TikTok-scrolling crowd who’d rather sip than chew.

To that end, they launched a whole new coffee chain that looked like Starbucks after a U-F-O abduction. It was called CosMc’s, which was pretty appropriate because – it wasn’t long for this world.

videos.title: When Did Campbell's Get Chunky?
videos.overview: Whether you’re taking care of a child with the sniffles or you’re just too lazy to cook for real, soup is a household staple. But it’s one largely dominated by a single name: Campbell’s. Only thanks to their brilliant marketing, you probably know it best as “Chunky.” Do You eat Campbell's Chunky? What do you think of Campbell's?

videos.title: What's The REAL Difference Between Carl's Jr. And Hardee's?
videos.overview: Have you ever looked at a Carl’s Jr. and a Hardee’s and thought, “Man those two franchises are a helluva lot alike”? Well… you’re not wrong. Those two chains are basically fast food siblings who share a face, but still insist they’re totally different people. Which have you eaten at? Do you prefer one over the other? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: The Soda That Had TOO MUCH Caffeine
videos.overview:
Before energy drinks ruled the world, there was Jolt Cola. Double the caffeine, all of the sugar, and none of the subtlety. In the mid eighties, Jolt didn’t just quietly launch, it exploded onto shelves like a punch in the face. It sparked panic, rebellion, and some of the most chaotic Gen X stories told.

So, let us know in the comments - Did you ever drink a Jolt Cola?

videos.title: Why Your Favorite Childhood Chocolate Became Illegal
videos.overview: For those lucky enough to live in a world where no candy is illegal, Kinder Surprise Eggs are a popular treat for chocolate lovers, toy collectors and egg aficionados alike. But in the U-S… they’re contraband. So why does everyone else get to chow down on this toy dispensing candy while Americans are left out?

videos.title: How Cinnabon Outlasted The Mall
videos.overview: You know that moment in a mall when you swear you’re just “cutting through” to get to something else, but then it hits you — the smell. A warm, sweet, buttery cloud that hovers like a cartoon hand beckoning you toward your fate. You weren’t hungry. You weren’t looking for dessert. And yet… resistance is futile! Have you ever eaten at Cinnabon? Give us YOUR thoughts in the comments!

videos.title: The Rise And Fall Of Snapple
videos.overview: In the world of fast food redheads, there’s Ronald McDonald, sometimes The Burger King – depending on which version you’re looking at – and there’s Wendy.And for decades, Wendy’s held their own as the number three burger chain in the United States. But the times, they may be a-changing.

videos.title: The Strange Soda Peru Chose Over Coca-Cola
videos.overview: When most people think of soda they think of things like Coke, Pepsi, Sprite and maybe some kind of Root Beer or Orange. What they don’t usually think of, is the Incas. Unless you’re talking about the people of Peru, who think of a local brand that did the impossible. So, have YOU ever had the pleasure of drinking this elusive soda? Where did you find it? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: The Cheesy Rise Of Stuffed Crust Pizza
videos.overview: In the high-stakes world of pizza, fast delivery times and better ingredients are always important, but the real way to grow your business is through new idea. And the biggest innovation in pizza since pre-sliced pepperoni is definitely the stuffed crust. But who really is responsible for the creation of this delectable delicacy?

videos.title: Why Food Dye HAD To Die
videos.overview: Food dye: once just a tool for cute elementary-school experiments, is now a surprising fixture in your everyday food. Though its recently been thrown into the spotlight, societies have been dying food and drink since the ancient Egyptian times (of not longer!). Today we look deep into dyes, why all the concern, and what is on the horizon for these ubiquitous dyes we all ingest! What do you think about food dyes?

videos.title: Milano Cookies Were Invented By Accident
videos.overview: If you’ve ever eaten a Milano cookie and thought, “This seems too elegant to have been invented on purpose…” Congratulations. You’re right. The Pepperidge Farm Milano is one of history’s greatest culinary whoopsies, right up there with the chocolate chip cookie!have you ever had Milano Cookies? Which is your favorite?

videos.title: The Strangest Canned Foods Ever Made
videos.overview: As a people, we have made some pretty great technological strides. The wheel, the printing press, the camera – all of them a great benefit to the entire human race. One that maybe doesn’t get spoken about enough though, is canned food. And much like the aforementioned advances, we’ve done some pretty strange stuff with it. What's the strangest thing you have ever seen canned? What is your favorite?

videos.title: Cheez-Its Aren't What You Think
videos.overview: They look like cheese. They smell like cheese. They kind of look like little slices of cheese. But if you’ve ever stared at a Cheez-It mid-snack and wondered what’s actually inside that tiny orange square — you’re not alone.What do you think about these little orange squares? Do you like a particular type of Cheez-It?

videos.title: Every Crazy Oreo Flavor We Could Find
videos.overview: Oreo cookies might just be the most consistently snackable treat in the junk food aisle. But after years of crumbling the competition with that fluffy, teeth-numbingly tasty cream, Oreo decided to get weird with it. Have you ever tried any of the wackiest flavors? If so, which was it?

videos.title: Why Wendy's Is Slowly Dying
videos.overview: In the world of fast food redheads, there’s Ronald McDonald, sometimes The Burger King – depending on which version you’re looking at – and there’s Wendy. And for decades, Wendy’s held their own as the number three burger chain in the United States. But the times, they may be a-changing. What do you think about Wendy's?

videos.title: How Bacon Became The King Of Breakfast
videos.overview:
There’s something strangely comforting about the sound of bacon sizzling in a pan. It’s not just cooking; it’s a little morning performance, a tiny ritual that tells your stomach the day has begun.

But as familiar as that moment feels, the truth is bacon isn’t just for the first meal of the day anymore. When d o YOU eat your bacon? What's your favorite way to consume bacon?

videos.title: Anthony Bourdain's Most Controversial Food Opinions
videos.overview: Anthony Bourdain didn’t just eat food — he used it to tell stories about power, culture, class, identity, and who really gets a seat at the table. Along the way, he developed some strong — and sometimes wildly unpopular — opinions about what people eat, how they eat, and why most of them are doing it wrong.

videos.title: Why Does Everyone Hate Arby's?
videos.overview: There are some things in life people have strong opinions about, including: religion, politics, and – apparently – Arby’s. For whatever reason, the world has drawn battle lines over whether the franchise is under-appreciated or if it should be shot into space, never to return. So, what do YOU think of Arby's? Have you ever eaten at one?

videos.title: A.1. Sauce Was Never intended For Steak. . .
videos.overview:
Have you ever looked at a bottle of A-1 sauce and thought, “What…are you?” Steak’s sidekick? Ketchup’s fancy cousin? A Victorian condiment that somehow survived the Industrial Revolution?

Well, if so… you’re far from alone. But even though most people don’t know exactly what A-1 is, every steak lover has an opinion on it.

videos.title: Did Taco Bell Steal The Best Idea They Ever Had?
videos.overview: There are plenty of wild fast-food mashups — but only one that feels like it was dreamed up at 2 a.m. in a dorm room and then somehow made a billion dollars. Yes, the Doritos Locos Taco was a pretty inspiring success story. At least, it was if the idea wasn’t stolen. But… was it?

videos.title: The Disgusting Truth About What Pirates Actually Ate
videos.overview: Once upon a time, the Caribbean was ruled by pirates cool enough to earn themselves a ride at Disneyland and a billion dollar movie franchise. But those movies don’t go into a lot of detail about what those pirates ate, or what they did when the food ran out.

videos.title: The Rise And Fall Of California Pizza Kitchen
videos.overview: You’d think taking a food known for being cheap and casual and trying to convince people it was haute cuisine would be a losing business strategy. But it was a winner for California Pizza Kitchen. Until it wasn’t.

videos.title: Are Frozen Fish Sticks Actually Fish?
videos.overview: When it comes to fish sticks, few brands have weathered more storms than Gorton’s. Which was your favorite brand?

videos.title: Whatever Happened To Shake 'N Bake?
videos.overview: Most foods are things you eat. Shake ’N Bake was something you did. It wasn’t just dinner, it was a ritual involving a plastic bag, raw chicken, and the kind of aggressive shaking that felt oddly therapeutic. Until… it wasn’t. So did you have Shake 'N Bake growing up? DId you help in that dinner prep?

videos.title: How A Publicity Stunt Nearly Destroyed IHOP
videos.overview:
For decades, IHOP was the place you went when you wanted pancakes, coffee, and maybe to make a few questionable life choices at 2 a.m. But behind the blue roofs and bottomless coffee is a story that starts with nuclear panic… and peaks with one of the internet’s most infamous marketing stunts.

What do you think of this stunt? Did you ever eat at IHOB? How was the burger?

videos.title: What Actually Is I Can't Believe It's Not Butter?
videos.overview: Once upon a time, someone tasted butter… and said, “what if this, but cheaper?”. That question birthed margarine, sparked lawsuits, fueled dairy conspiracies, and eventually led to one of the most iconic food names of the twentieth century — a product that’s almost butter, almost margarine, and absolutely confusing.

videos.title: The Rise And Fall Of The "Set It And Forget it" Empire
videos.overview: Other than a certain cartoon detective, there’s nowhere we love gadgets more than in our kitchens… and perhaps no one is more responsible for those tools than Ron Popeil. He’s the ever-smilling pitchman whose specialized doohickeys turned the television infomercial from a programming afterthought into a cultural institution.

videos.title: The Coffee Chain That Came Out Of Nowhere To Challenge Starbucks
videos.overview: 7 Brew enters the chat as the newest player trying to muscle its way into the crowded American caffeine coliseum. In just a few short years, the brand has positioned itself as a fast-rising, hyper-energetic alternative to Starbucks. Despite being relatively young, 7 Brew has already built a reputation for speed, personality, and a menu that essentially says, “We do what we do well, and then THAT’S IT.”

videos.title: The Fake Brand That Made Costco Billions
videos.overview: Costco is a magical place. You walk in for paper towels, and walk out with a kayak, a ten-pound bag of quinoa, and a heaping plate of panic over where you’re going to store it all. But no matter what you buy, chances are it has one familiar name on it: Kirkland Signature. People trust it. Like… deeply. Religiously even. Possibly more than they trust some relatives! Do You buy Kirkland products? If so, what do you think about em?

videos.title: Why Ginger Ale Tastes Better On Airplanes
videos.overview:
Ever notice how airplane food tastes… weird? You board the plane starving, open that tiny tray table meal, take one bite, and suddenly wonder if your taste buds stayed back at the airport gate.

Believe it or not, it’s not just the airline food quality… and it’s not just you. There’s actually a scientific reason airplane food tastes different at 35,000 feet. From cabin pressure, to dry air, flying can seriously mess with how your brain tastes food. So what’s the deal with airline meals, and why do they taste so bland in the sky?

Have you ever had airplane food that was actually good? What airline was it, and what did you eat?

videos.title: How Skyline Chili Worked When It Absolutely Should Have Failed
videos.overview: For most of the world, chili is thick, spicy, and eaten with a spoon. But in Cincinnati, they looked at that tradition and thought: What if we poured it over spaghetti, added cinnamon, and built an entire food culture around it? Welcome to the strange and legendary world of Cincinnati chili—a uniquely Midwestern dish made famous by restaurants like Skyline Chili. Instead of a bowl, it’s served on a plate of spaghetti and topped with towering piles of shredded cheese, onions, and beans in carefully ordered combinations known as “3-ways,” “4-ways,” and “5-ways.”

videos.title: Why McDonald's Killed The Snack Wrap (Then Brought It Back)
videos.overview:
The McDonald’s Snack Wrap was the perfect middle ground between a “lighter” fast food option and the kind of late-night creation you’d expect after a Jay and Silent Bob movie marathon. Small, cheap, and ridiculously addictive, it quickly became one of the most beloved items on the McDonald’s menu.

The original McDonald’s Snack Wrap packed big flavor into a soft flour tortilla: crisp lettuce, shredded cheddar and Monterey Jack cheese, your choice of sauces, and most importantly a juicy strip of chicken. That chicken came straight from the same legendary supply used for the fan-favorite McDonald’s Chicken Selects, which were hugely popular at the time.

So how did one of the most popular McDonald’s menu items end up disappearing from restaurants?

videos.title: The Oldest Cola In The World is Not Coke
videos.overview:
Before the Coca-Cola vs. Pepsi cola wars took over the world, another soda was already making history. On Colombia’s Caribbean coast, a mysterious bright pink drink was bubbling into existence decades before the big soda brands battled for dominance — and it’s still popular today.

Today on Weird History Food, we dive into the forgotten origins of Colombia’s iconic pink soda Kola Roman, including the surprising story behind its invention, and how it survived the global takeover of the cola giants. From regional tradition to cult favorite, this unusual soft drink proves that the history of soda is stranger — and sweeter — than you might think! So tell us in the comments - have you ever had Kola Roman? What do you think of it?

If you love food history, unusual drinks, and forgotten food stories, hit subscribe for more episodes of Weird History Food.

videos.title: The Disastrous Downfall Of Boston Market
videos.overview:
Before meal kits, before DoorDash, and long before cheap grocery store rotisserie chickens, Boston Market was a real presence. It promised comfort food classics—like Thanksgiving dinner any day of the week—without the cooking, cleanup, or family drama! At its peak, this fast-casual chain was booming, redefining how Americans ate homestyle meals on the go. But almost as quickly as it rose, Boston Market began to collapse.

So what went wrong? From rapid expansion and massive debt to changing food trends and fierce competition, this is the strange rise and fall of one of America’s most iconic comfort food chains.

videos.title: How An Ice Cream Topping Became A Kids' Drink
videos.overview:
Hawaiian Punch has been around forever—or at least it feels that way. Bright red, ultra-sweet, and somehow tasting like “fruit” without being tied to any one fruit, it’s a drink that defined childhood for millions. But what is Hawaiian Punch, really? And where did it come from?

Today on Weird History, we dive into the surprising origins of Hawaiian Punch: H it became a lunchroom staple, and what’s actually behind that iconic flavor. From its unexpected beginnings, to its rise as a sugary pop culture legend, this is the story you never knew you needed about a drink you probably never questioned. Did you ever drink this magical concoction? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: The Lie Behind V8
videos.overview:
You think V8 is healthy… but is it really?

Picture this: you’re in the grocery store, determined to make better choices. You skip the soda, avoid sugary sports drinks, and reach for something that feels responsible: V8. Packed with vegetables, it has to be good for you… right? Well… not so fast.

In this episode of Weird History, we dig into the surprising origins of V8, the truth behind its “healthy” reputation, and the hidden details most people never question. From clever marketing to nutritional gray areas, the story of this iconic drink is a lot more complicated than it seems.

Is V8 actually good for you? Or is that just really good branding?

videos.title: The Slow, Sad Death Of Pizza
videos.overview:
Pizza is cheap, comforting, and available everywhere… or at least it used to be. But recently, something strange has been happening. America’s favorite food seems to be slowly fading away, and after you hear the reasons why, you may never look at a slice the same way again.

From rising costs to changing tastes, this episode of Weird History Food takes a deep dive into the surprising truth behind pizza’s quiet decline and what it reveals about how America eats today.

videos.title: The Inevitable Downfall Of Jack In The Box
videos.overview:
While McDonald’s, Burger King, and Wendy’s dominate the fast-food burger world, Jack in the Box has long been carving out a surprising legacy of its own. From its creepy clown mascot to the iconic Jumbo Jack, Jack in the Box seemingly has everything it needs to compete at the top... but lately, things haven't been going so well for Jack.

In this episode of Weird History, we dive into the strange rise and fall of one of America’s most unique and unforgettable fast food chains.

videos.title: Is Da' Bomb Actually The Hottest Hot Sauce In The World?
videos.overview:
Think you can handle Da’ Bomb? Well, think again! The infamous #8 hot sauce from Hot Ones is so incredibly spicy it’s manufacturer warns people against eating it straight. So why does Hot Ones host Sean Evans have celebrities like Sabrina Carpenter taking it head-on?

In this episode of Weird History Food, we give you a glimpse of the shocking truth behind one of the most feared and misunderstood hot sauces on YouTube, discuss how it became a viral challenge, and try to figure out why famous people keep letting it destroy their taste buds.

videos.title: Why THIS Became The Most Hated Bottled Water
videos.overview:
In the late 1990s, Americans started turning away from sugary soda and embracing what seemed like a healthier alternative: bottled water. Sensing the massive shift in consumer habits, Coca-Cola jumped into the booming market in 1999 with Dasani.

But what followed wasn’t so much a success story as it was a branding disaster. From its controversial sourcing to its unusual taste, Dasani triggered a public backlash and quickly became one of the most criticized bottled water brands ever.

So how did one of the world’s biggest companies get it so wrong? And why do people still talk about Dasani today?

videos.title: Why Sliced Bread Used To Be Controversial
videos.overview:
Ever wondered why amazing new innovations are always referred to as “the greatest thing since sliced bread”?

In this Weird History deep dive, we uncover the surprising origin story behind sliced bread, discuss how it revolutionized everyday life and explain why it became the gold standard for innovation.

From the disaster that forced its inventor to invent it twice, to the rise of Wonder Bread, to the World War 2 era ban that took sliced bread off supermarket shelves, this is the strange, fascinating story of how a simple loaf changed the world forever.

videos.title: What Exactly Is Worcestershire Sauce?
videos.overview:
Worcestershire sauce: It's salty, tangy, funky, fishy and almost impossible to spell or pronounce. But while you’ve almost certainly tasted it... do you actually know what’s in it?

One of the oldest bottled sauces in America, this mysterious condiment turns up everywhere from burgers to Bloody Marys and it has a history that’s far stranger than you’d expect.

So on this episode of Weird History Food, we're going to try and answer the questions: What is Worcestershire sauce and how did it become a kitchen staple? And by the time we're done, we guarantee you’ll never look at that bottle the same way again.

videos.title: How A Random Burger King In Pittsburgh Went Rogue
videos.overview:
From the U-K's "Dominic's Pizza" to Iran's "Pizza Hat" to China's "7-12", knock off fast food places are far more common than most Americans realize. But the strange Burger King that briefly existed on the south side of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania wasn't just an imitation with a deceptively similar name, it was an outright counterfeit.

The building said Burger King, the uniforms said Burger King, and so did the receipts, but when employees started telling customers they were out of items like Whoppers, and food started being served in plain brown lunch bags and dixie cups, locals began to realize that something was up.

So on this episode of Weird History Food, we're going to get to the bottom of what was going on at the infamous rogue Burger King of Pittsburgh.

videos.title: The Strange Disappearance Of McDonald’s Old Bay Filet-O-Fish
videos.overview:
The Old Bay Filet-O-Fish was a simple twist on a classic McDonald’s sandwich. The limited-time menu item, which featured the iconic Filet-O-Fish topped with bold Old Bay-seasoned tartar sauce, exploded in popularity, became an overnight fan obsession, and then vanished just as quickly.

So why did McDonald’s pull the Old Bay Filet-O-Fish? Was it a supply issue, a marketing experiment, or something else entirely? And of course, the biggest question of all: will it ever come back?

In this episode of Weird History, we break down the meteoric rise and mysterious disappearance of one of McDonald’s most talked-about limited releases, explore the fan reaction, and uncover what really happened to the Old Bay Filet-O-Fish.

videos.title: The $1 Food Court Battle: Costco vs Sam’s Club
videos.overview:
With prices constantly on the rise, everybody's on the lookout for a good, cheap meal, and while Costco’s famous $1.50 hot dog combo has a cult following… Sam’s Club may be quietly undercutting them.

So in this episode of Weird History, we're pitting the two warehouse superstore food courts against each other to determine whose meal is the better deal.

Check out our breakdown and then jump into the comments and let us know which food court wins the war for your wallet.

videos.title: The Rise And Fall Of Frozen Orange Juice
videos.overview:
Minute Maid frozen orange juice is a grocery store classic with a surprising history. A freezer aisle staple since the late 1940s, frozen orange juice concentrate has long been helping families get their daily dose of vitamin C quickly and affordably. But recently, Minute Maid has chosen to discontinue the product leaving loyal customers wondering... why?

In this episode of Weird History, we dive into the fascinating story behind frozen orange juice, from its unexpected origins, to its cultural impact, to the reasons it may not be as popular today.

videos.title: The Strange Genius Of Wendy’s Chili
videos.overview:
Wendy’s sells over 83 MILLION servings of chili every year; enough to fill more than eight Olympic-sized swimming pools. But the real story isn’t how much they sell… it’s what’s in it.

On this episode of Weird History Food, we're taking a look at the surprisingly clever fast food secret behind Wendy's chili and how Dave Thomas figured out he could turn his garbage into his secret weapon.

videos.title: How Grey Poupon Became The Mustard Of Rich People
videos.overview:
The idea that someone's personality can be judged solely by what condiments they put on their food sounds ridiculous, but one mustard brand actually convinced an entire nation it was possible… and people bought into it. But how did a simple condiment reshape identity, class, and culture? And why did it work so well?

In this episode of Weird History, we dive into the surprisingly effective marketing campaign and strange psychology that turned Grey Poupon Dijon Mustard into an unlikely status symbol.

videos.title: The Weirdest Foods Ever Put in A Can
videos.overview: As a people, we have made some pretty great technological strides like the wheel, the printing press, and the camera. One that maybe doesn’t get spoken about enough though, is canned food. And much like the aforementioned advances, we’ve done some pretty strange stuff with it.

videos.title: How Hershey's Ruined Reese's
videos.overview:
In February of 2026, the grandson of H.B. Reese, founder of Reese's Candy Company, publicly criticized Hershey’s, accusing the company of replacing core ingredients with cheaper substitutes; a claim Hershey's didn't even bother to deny.

In this episode of Weird History, we dig into the growing controversy over alleged ingredient changes in popular chocolate bars. Are beloved sweets being quietly downgraded? From recipe shifts to consumer backlash, here’s what’s really going on behind the wrappers.

videos.title: The Disastrous Downfall of KFC
videos.overview:
For decades, Kentucky Fried Chicken dominated the fast food scene with the top secret fried chicken recipe created by its larger-than-life founder, Colonel Harlan Sanders. But more recently, KFC has struggled to keep people interested in what it's selling.

In this episode of Weird History Food, we dig through the corporate battles, declining quality, and broken branding to figure out exactly how one of America’s most beloved restaurant chains lost its way.

videos.title: Everything That Went Wrong For Tim Hortons
videos.overview:
To Canadians, Tim Hortons is more than a coffee shop; it's a symbol of Canada itself. From hockey culture to political campaigns, “Timmies” was seemingly everywhere. But behind the double-doubles and Timbits, the company has found itself facing controversy, consumer complaints about declining quality, angry franchise owners, and a major identity crisis.

In this episode of Weird History Food, we head north to take a good hard look at everything that's gone wrong for Tim Hortons.

videos.title: Everything That Went Wrong For Salt Bae
videos.overview:
Thanks to a viral video showing off his unusually stylish meat slicing technique and now legendary salt sprinkle, the Turkish butcher and restauranteur Nusret Gökçe shot to fame as "Salt Bae." But thanks to a series of mistakes, missteps, and plain old bad decisions, the internet's love affair with Gökçe proved short-lived.

In this episode of Weird History Food, we're peeling back the hype to take a look at the bizarre rise and fall of the world’s most dramatic chef.

videos.title: Which Orange Soda Is The Definitive Orange Soda?
videos.overview: Orange soda is bright, bubbly, and more popular than you'd think. But which one is the sweetest? Or the fizziest? And why are they all the exact same orange as a traffic cone? In this episode of Weird History Food we’re ranking the wild world of orange soda, from Fanta to Sunkist to Crush, to find out which one truly reigns supreme. What's your favorite orange soda? Jump into the comments and let us know.

videos.title: The Strange Cult Of Whataburger
videos.overview:
In the state of Texas, Whataburger is more than a regional fast food chain, it's a beloved institution that people defend like a member of the family. But what exactly is it about this seemingly run of the mill burger joint that inspired such cult-like devotion?

In this episode of Weird History Food, we peek behind the orange-and-white stripes to figure out how Whataburger survived viral scandals, fierce competition, and backlash over major corporate changes to become one of America’s most beloved regional burger chains.

videos.title: Why Hi-C Ecto Cooler Never Should Have Worked
videos.overview:
Originally launched as a Ghostbusters-themed Hi-C drink in the 1980s, Ecto Cooler became one of the most beloved kids beverages of all time. It even survived for a while after the Ghostbusters franchise faded away. Nonetheless, Hi-C eventually discontinued it and that should’ve been the end... but it wasn't.

On this episode of Weird History Food, we're taking a look at how Ecto Cooler became a pop culture legend that fans kept bringing back from the dead.

videos.title: How Werther’s Accidentally Became For Old People
videos.overview:
Werther’s Original candies are known for their rich caramel flavor, their wholesome ingredients and their gold wrappers. But what they're most famous for is being the unofficial candy of senior citizens everywhere.

In this episode of Weird History Food, we explain how Werther’s Originals became the ultimate “grandparent candy,” and examine whether that association turned out to be a good thing or a bad thing in the long run.

videos.title: Army Food Is Better Than You Think...
videos.overview:
From prehistoric battles to today's high-tech military conflicts, war has shaped human civilization for thousands of years. But one challenge has never changed: soldiers need food. Long before modern MREs (Meals Ready-to-Eat), armies relied on everything from dried meat and hardtack to canned rations designed to survive the harshest battlefields. Some of those meals were barely edible, while others became surprisingly beloved by the troops who relied on them.

In this episode of Weird History, we're tracing the fascinating evolution of military rations from the through the ages. What did George Washington's soldiers eat? How did armies feed millions of soldiers during world wars? And are modern military rations actually tastier than their reputation suggests?

videos.title: How Goldfish Became America’s Favorite Cracker
videos.overview: Pepperidge Farm's Goldfish have been on supermarket shelves since 1963, so you might think people would be tired of them, but that doesn't seem to be the case. On the contrary, Goldfish are now the fastest growing cracker brand in the United States. In this episode of Weird History Food we take a look at how one woman's quest to find snacks her son could safely eat led to one of the most iconic crackers in history, and the simple, yet clever strategy Pepperidge Farm has used to keep Goldfish so popular generation after generation.

videos.title: The Real Reason People Love Aldi Isn’t What You Think...
videos.overview:
A grocery store where you have to pay to use a shopping cart. No familiar brands. No background music. And products with names that seem impossible to pronounce. It sounds like a grocery store designed by aliens, but it's actually Aldi, the discount supermarket that grew from a small German family business into one -- or actually two -- of the most successful and beloved grocery chains in the world.

On this episode of Weird History Food we're taking a look at how a store that breaks almost every rule of modern grocery shopping became a global retail phenomenon. From its unusual shopping carts and private-label products to its ruthless cost-cutting strategies and billion-dollar success story, this is the weird history of Aldi.

videos.title: Why One Fast Food Chain Has Two Names
videos.overview: The merger of Checkers and Rally’s was supposed to create a fast-food powerhouse. But instead... it nearly destroyed both brands. On this episode of Weird History Food From we're looking at the bizarre story of Checkers and Rally’s and how the combined franchises went from bankruptcy scares to a drive-thru success.

videos.title: What Happened To SoBe?
videos.overview:
Back in the nineties, you could find SoBe teas, fruit-juice blends and enhanced water beverages in almost every convenience store cooler in America. Then, one day... SoBe just vanished.

In this episode of Weird History, we're taking a look at the strange rise and sudden fall of SoBe, along with other drinks that once ruled store shelves before disappearing from public memory. Did you like SoBe? Let us know in the comments.

videos.title: Why Did Everyone Think Pop Rocks Could Kill You?
videos.overview:
From mouth-scorching hot sauces to tongue-twisting sour candies, people have always been drawn to foods that push the limits. But few treats have sparked fear, controversy, or urban legends like Pop Rocks. For decades, rumors claimed the explosive candy could literally make your stomach burst. Parents panicked, kids spread the word, and the tale became one of the most famous food myths of all-time.

In this episode of Weird History, we're diving into the surprising origins of Pop Rocks, the stomach-explosion rumor that wouldn't die, and the surprising truth behind one of the most misunderstood candies ever created.

videos.title: What Exactly Is HP Sauce?
videos.overview: For generations, HP Sauce has been a staple on English breakfast tables, slathered on bacon sandwiches, sausages, and meat pies. Yet despite its popularity, most people have no idea what the "HP" in the name actually stands for.

videos.title: What Happened To Long John Silver’s?
videos.overview:
Long John Silver's built its reputation on crispy fried seafood, but after years of struggling, it made a surprising move: adding chicken to the menu. Why would a seafood restaurant bet big on chicken? And could it save one of America's most recognizable fast-food chains from drowning?

In this episode of Weird History Food, we dive into the history of Long John Silver's to try and make sense out of its rise, decline, and the unexpected menu changes that may just turn the tide.

videos.title: How Many Licks Does It ACTUALLY Take To Get To The Center of A Tootsie Pop?
videos.overview:
In the history of the world, few questions have puzzled humanity as deeply as "How many licks does it take to get to the Tootsie Roll center of a Tootsie Pop?" First posed by a cartoon boy to a series of cartoon animals in a 1969 commercial, the now-iconic question became an instant part of pop culture, and eventually, an object of inquiry for scientists and universities all over the world.

In this episode of Weird History Food, we unwrap the fascinating history and surprising science behind one of America's most iconic candies, and in the process, try to discover exactly how many licks it takes to get to the tootsie roll center.

videos.title: Why People Pay a Fortune to Eat Fish Eggs
videos.overview:
Caviar is the luxury food that made generations of kids say, "You eat fish eggs?!" Despite that reaction, it's been one of the world's most expensive and sought-after delicacies for centuries, served to royalty, billionaires, and fine-dining enthusiasts.

On this episode of Weird History Food, we dig into this history to figure out how fish eggs became a global symbol of wealth and luxury... and the story is even stranger than you might expect.

videos.title: The History of Wendy's Frosty
videos.overview:
When most people hear the word "Frosty," they think of either a magical snowman... or the famous Wendy's Frosty. It was one of the original five menu items when Dave Thomas opened the very first Wendy's restaurant in 1969, and over fifty years later, it's still a fast-food icon. But what's the real story behind this legendary frozen dessert?

In this episode of Weird History, we're diving into the surprising history of the Wendy's Frosty, from its original recipe and creation to the secrets behind its signature texture, its biggest flavor changes, and how it became one of the most recognizable fast-food desserts ever made.

videos.title: 8 Fast Food Places You Thought Were Dead (But Aren’t)
videos.overview:
If you watch Weird History Food, you know that plenty of fast food places have crashed, burned, and vanished. But some of the most famous chains you probably assumed were gone... never actually disappeared.

On this episode of Weird History Food, we take a look at the iconic burger joints and nostalgic restaurant brands that are still in business... even if they're hiding in plain sight.

videos.title: The Well Deserved Death Of Heart Attack Grill
videos.overview:
After more than 20 years of shocking tourists on the Las Vegas Strip, the infamous Heart Attack Grill, known for its massive burgers, hospital theme, and "eat yourself to death" marketing, suddenly closed its doors in May of 2026. For decades, the restaurant proudly embraced controversy with its famous Quadruple Bypass Burger, nurses, wheelchairs, and over-the-top gimmicks, but when the iconic Las Vegas institution unexpectedly shut down, the real reason had nothing to do with its notorious menu.

On this episode of Weird History Food, we explore the rise, scandals, health controversies, and surprising downfall of one of Las Vegas's most unforgettable dining experiences as we try to discover what exactly happened to the Heart Attack Grill.

videos.title: The Evolution of Astronaut Food
videos.overview:
Everyone knows that traveling into space raises a lot of difficult issues, for example: How do you feed a human in zero gravity? Crumbs can damage equipment, liquids float away, and every meal has to survive launch while providing enough nutrition to keep astronauts alive millions of miles from Earth.

In this episode of Weird History Food, we explore the strange, surprising history of space food, from freeze-dried meals to the science behind eating in orbit. Discover how NASA solved one of the most unexpected problems of human spaceflight, and why feeding astronauts remains a challenge more than 75 years after the dawn of the Space Age.

videos.title: Weird Fast Food Items From Around The World
videos.overview:
Think you know your favorite fast food chains? Think again. Around the world, restaurants like Domino's, McDonald's, Burger King, and others serve some of the strangest menu items you could possibly imagine. From a snake pizza to burgers topped with chocolate sauce, these international fast food creations prove that every country truly has its own unique take on comfort food.

In this episode of Weird History Food, we explore the weirdest fast food menu items from around the world, uncovering bizarre international specialties, limited-time offerings, and regional favorites that will leave you wondering, "Who actually ordered this?"
